package cache

import "time"

var now = time.Now

type entry struct {
	value int
	setAt time.Time
	used  time.Time
}

type Cache struct {
	capacity int
	ttl      time.Duration
	items    map[string]*entry
}

func New(capacity int, ttl time.Duration) *Cache {
	return &Cache{capacity: capacity, ttl: ttl, items: map[string]*entry{}}
}

func (c *Cache) expired(e *entry) bool { return now().Sub(e.setAt) > c.ttl }

// dropExpired removes what the cache no longer holds. Expiry and the
// size limit are the same question: an entry that has expired is gone,
// so it cannot be occupying room or competing for recency.
func (c *Cache) dropExpired() {
	for k, e := range c.items {
		if c.expired(e) {
			delete(c.items, k)
		}
	}
}

func (c *Cache) Set(key string, value int) {
	c.dropExpired()
	if _, replacing := c.items[key]; !replacing && len(c.items) >= c.capacity {
		c.evict()
	}
	at := now()
	c.items[key] = &entry{value: value, setAt: at, used: at}
}

func (c *Cache) evict() {
	var oldest string
	var at time.Time
	for k, e := range c.items {
		if oldest == "" || e.used.Before(at) {
			oldest, at = k, e.used
		}
	}
	if oldest != "" {
		delete(c.items, oldest)
	}
}

func (c *Cache) Get(key string) (int, bool) {
	e, ok := c.items[key]
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	if c.expired(e) {
		delete(c.items, key)
		return 0, false
	}
	e.used = now()
	return e.value, true
}

func (c *Cache) Len() int {
	c.dropExpired()
	return len(c.items)
}
